newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea apologises for submarine incursion.
newsitem.headline: North Korea apologises for submarine incursion.

text.p: North Korea formally apologised for the first time on Sunday for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korean waters in September.

The apology, in a statement from a North Korean foreign ministry spokesman and carried by the official Korean Central News Agency monitored in Tokyo, expressed "deep regret for the submarine incident" and promised no repetitions.

"The spokesman of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the DPRK is authorised to express deep regret for the submarine incident in the coastal waters of Kangnung, South Korea, in September, 1996, that caused the tragic loss of human life," KCNA said in a brief report.
"The DPRK will make efforts to ensure that such an incident will not recur and will work with others for durable peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula."

The incursion, in which 26 heavily armed North Koreans were landed on a beach on the east coast of South Korea, hampered efforts to improve relations between the two Koreas. It also halted progress on four-party talks proposed by the United States and South Korea with the North and China on a lasting peace to replace the truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

South Korea demanded an apology as the price of resuming aid to the North and implementing a 1994 agreement between Washington and Pyongyang under which it will supply nuclear reactors to North Korea.
